chapter_seo_title: Li Huowang's Frustration Boils in Chapter 337 of Dao Gui Yi Xian
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang chokes on his rage after being tricked into killing an innocent man. As he stalks the Bone Buddha Temple, he realizes the Chief Recorder's golden abacus is not hunting people—it's hunting something else.
og_title: Chapter 337: The Abacus – A Bureaucratic Nightmare
og_description: Li Huowang must work alongside the man who made him a killer. As the search for the Zuowandao grows strange, he begins to suspect the eunuch holding the leash knows far more than he's letting on.
twitter_title: The real monster isn't the Zuowandao; it's the system.
twitter_description: Li Huowang's rage is a cage. The Chief Recorder doesn't explain. The mission doesn't make sense. And he just hesitated at the worst possible moment.

lore_anchors.definition: A temple dedicated to housing a relic of the Buddha; in the Dao-Twisted World, it is a site of the Supervisory Heavenly Office's current operation.
A high-ranking eunuch official in the Supervisory Heavenly Office, wielding both bureaucratic and supernatural power.
A supernatural diagnostic tool used by the Chief Recorder to detect metaphysical discrepancies, not just for counting money.
A set of supernormal abilities attributed to accomplished Buddhist practitioners, including clairvoyance, clairaudience, and knowledge of others' thoughts; Xinchi's claim to have them is now suspect.
A powerful 'military path' weapon that is both a tool and a corrupting influence, now carried by Li Huowang.
The traditional patchwork robe worn by Buddhist monks, signifying their vows and order; the abbot's ornate kasaya contrasts with the temple's troubled situation.
A heavy wooden board locked around the neck and hands, used as a portable pillory in imperial China; Xinchi wears one as a punishment.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is Li Huowang so angry?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He was forced to kill an innocent person because the monk Xinchi gave a faulty identification. The monk's casual dismissal of the error is what truly infuriates him.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the Chief Recorder doing with his abacus?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He isn't looking for people; he is using the abacus as a supernatural diagnostic tool to calculate a metaphysical discrepancy in the temple's 'balance sheet' or structure.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Who is the Knife-Promise Man (Hong Da)?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He is a member of the Supervisory Heavenly Office team, a pragmatic and experienced agent who tells Li Huowang to stop overthinking and just follow orders.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the 'handle' Xinchi warned about?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It refers to a stealth attack or a threat from a specific direction, likely from a hidden Zuowandao agent. Li Huowang's hesitation caused him to miss the opportunity to act.
